note: LONGER onboarding research (2026-11-25). Store host: www.longer.net (Shopify, myshopify longer-net; the Awin default link for program 75738 redirects there, and longer3d.com 301s there too). It is one global store priced in USD (storefront country HK) with 'Fast & Free Shipping over $49 in US & EU'; no separate US storefront. Resin was the brief's ask, but every resin printer on the store (Orange 4K, Orange 10, Orange 30) and the Wash & Cure machine were sold out in all variants on 2026-11-25, as were the LK4 Pro, LK4 X, LK1 and Cube 2 FDM printers, so the 3D-printer pick is the in-stock LK10 Plus FDM printer and the 3d-printer category's FDM label needs no change. laser-engraver already exists in CATEGORIES. Picks: Ray5 10W (most-reviewed product, 292 store reviews), Ray7 20W (newer flagship, featured on the homepage and Black Friday page), Ray5 miniS 2.5W (cheapest enclosed/Class 1 machine) and LK10 Plus. Codes: LONGER prints spend-tier Black Friday codes BF5-BF20 on its sale page and every product page; the two pages give different thresholds (product pages: BF5 all orders, BF6 $299+, BF7 $899+, BF8 $1,999+, BF9 $3,999+, BF15 $6,999+, BF20 $9,999+; sale page: BF6 $899+, BF7 $1,999+ ... with BF20 shown without a threshold). Cart tests 2026-11-25 (control code rejected on all four): BF6 applied at $419.99 and $429.99, so the cart follows the product pages' $299 threshold. Best code: Ray5 10W BF5 $239.99 -> $228.00; Ray5 miniS BF5 $129.99 -> $123.50; Ray7 20W BF6 $429.99 -> $404.20; LK10 Plus BF6 $419.99 -> $394.80; BF7-BF20 rejected below their thresholds (not tested above them). records.warranty: 12 months on the laser module, motherboard, touch screen, motor and power adapter, and 3 months on wearing parts such as rollers, belts and cables, counted from the date of receipt; only for machines bought through LONGER's own channels, with proof of purchase.
records.returns: LONGER accepts returns within 30 days of delivery with the original receipt, if the product, packaging and materials are intact and the machine has been used fewer than 50 times; a service fee (percentage not stated by LONGER) is deducted from the refund, and separately bought materials cannot be returned. records.summary: LONGER's best-reviewed open-frame diode laser, a 10 W machine with a 400 × 400 mm bed that LONGER rates to cut 8 mm basswood in one pass. It works with LightBurn and LaserGRBL and costs $239.99 in LONGER's Black Friday sale.
records.fit: Suits a first-time hobbyist who wants to engrave and cut wood, leather and dark acrylic on a budget and can run it in a ventilated garage or workshop. Buyers who need an enclosure for indoor use should look at the WECREAT Vista 10W enclosed laser ($490 at WECREAT), and anyone who mainly wants thicker cuts should consider the Ray5 20W ($359.99 at LONGER).
caveats: $239.99 is LONGER's Black Friday price, which the store says runs until December 2, 2026; the product page shows $329.99 as the regular price.
LONGER's product page says the 5 W and 10 W Ray5 come without limit switches (sold separately), so automatic homing is not included, although the page's safety list includes limit-switch protection.

It is an open-frame diode laser with no enclosure (LONGER does not state a laser class for the Ray5), so smoke must be vented and eye protection worn; air assist is not in the Basic Set (the $299.99 10W Cutting Kit adds air assist and a honeycomb bed).
LONGER's own pages disagree on speed: the description says up to 24,000 mm/min, the spec table gives 10,000 mm/min for the 10 W (24,000 only for the separate 40 W).

Notebookcheck's review of an earlier 5.5 W Ray5 (Marc Herter, 2021) called its noise level rather high, found the rubber feet let it slip during fast moves, and said LONGER had cut some corners to reach the price.
Machine weight and overall dimensions are not stated by LONGER.

records.summary: A small preassembled laser engraver with Class 1 protection and a 130 × 140 mm work area, meant for engraving tags, coasters, leather and small wood pieces at home. The 2.5 W version costs $129.99 in LONGER's Black Friday sale.
records.fit: Suits a beginner or gift buyer who wants to personalize small items with a low-power laser that works over Wi-Fi or an app. It is an engraver first: anyone who wants to cut wood or acrylic, or engrave larger pieces, should buy a 10 W or 20 W open-frame machine such as the LONGER Ray5 10W ($239.99 at LONGER).
caveats: $129.99 is LONGER's Black Friday price, which the store says runs until December 2, 2026; the product page shows $269.99 as the regular price.
The 130 × 140 mm work area fits small items only, and LONGER gives no cutting thickness for the miniS; 2.5 W is mainly for engraving.

LONGER's product page says 'Class I safety protection' but does not describe the enclosure or a lid sensor; LONGER's January 2026 launch release calls it a fully enclosed engraver with FDA Class 1 certification.
On metal, LONGER's FAQ limits it to coated or treated metals.
Only 3 customer reviews on LONGER's store on 2026-11-25, and no independent hands-on review of the miniS was found.
LONGER does not say what the $219.99 Pro bundle adds over the Basic set.

records.summary: A large open-frame FDM printer with a 320 × 320 × 400 mm build volume, Klipper firmware and eddy-current auto leveling, rated up to 500 mm/s. It costs $419.99 in LONGER's Black Friday sale, and the smaller 225 mm LK10 is $299.99.

LONGER does not state nozzle or bed temperatures, the motion system, Wi-Fi or other connectivity, the bundled slicer, or printer size and weight.
It is an open-frame printer with no enclosure, so ABS and ASA, which LONGER lists as supported, are harder to print without warping or fumes.
